subject: Service handoff: reroute steps and customer verification (US/EU/APAC)
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-retail.com>, ops@acme-retail.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service handoff: reroute steps and customer verification (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Sarah / Acme ops team,

Quick update and immediate mitigation steps. We detected a localized peering disruption affecting Redwood’s regional gateway clusters in US-EAST and EU-WEST, which caused elevated 5xx rates and increased tail latency for requests routed through those gateways. APAC saw intermittent degradation due to propagation delays in the global routing table.

Impact summary:
- Affected regions: US (us-east), EU (eu-west); APAC saw transient degradation.
- Symptom: elevated 503/504, token timeouts, delayed streaming responses.
- Window: began ~2029-04-11 08:45 PDT; mitigation in progress.

Immediate customer-facing mitigation (please follow the checklist attached):
1) Switch to explicit regional endpoints (preferred) — example: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?preferred_region=us-central
   - This pins request routing to the selected regional cluster and avoids cross-region peering paths.
2) Reduce client DNS TTL to 30s while we validate reroute (we recommend 30s for the next 2 hours).
3) If you rely on a single shared endpoint, add the header X-Redwood-Prefer: region=us-central (or region=eu-west / apac-sg) to force region-local routing.
4) Validate with a quick smoke test (curl):
   - curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?preferred_region=us-central" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"prompt":"ping"}'
   - Confirm HTTP 200 and look for header X-Redwood-Trace: <trace-id>
5) If you see >1% 5xx after switching, attach one trace-id and timestamp and we’ll escalate immediately.

We’ve attached a step-by-step reroute checklist (reroute-checklist.xlsx) and opened a temporary SLA bridge (temporary-sla-bridge.pdf) while the networking team completes root-cause validation.

Requested customer action:
- Confirm when you have switched clients to preferred_region and run the smoke test (paste trace-id).
- If you cannot change the client quickly, let us know and we’ll provision a short-lived regional ingress for your account (automated edge mapping).

Next steps from Redwood:
- Marissa is coordinating traffic canaries to verify the alternate paths and will update once BGP preference changes have fully propagated.
- We’ll schedule a post-incident review with your team; invite attached (postmortem-invite.ics).

I’m standing by on this thread and we’ll keep updates frequent until resolved.

—
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 09:45:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Service handoff: reroute steps and customer verification (US/EU/APAC)

Evelyn — quick internal update on actions taken and ask for ops team.

What we’ve done so far:
- Deployed BGP preference override for affected edge POPs (targeted to us-east and eu-west). Propagation is ~5–12 minutes; we’re monitoring delta RTT and packet loss.
- Initiated continuous canary traffic to the alternate regional endpoints for Acme (ID: ACME-2028-RED-34-canary).
- Enabled a temporary lower-cost quantized exec path for non-sensitive traffic to reduce tail latency while routes converge.

Ask / Next steps:
- Markus: please confirm network team has added the ACL exception so Acme’s short-lived regional ingress can be provisioned if they request it.
- Ops: if Acme reports >1% 5xx after switching, escalate to network-oncall and paste trace-id.
- I uploaded the temporary SLA bridge doc to the thread; I’ve also set a short hold on credits in case we need to provide a one-time credit for the window.

Forwarding customer reply — Sarah will validate TTL behavior and CDN purge. If they cannot purge, we should offer the header-based prefer_region approach as primary.

—
Marissa Cole
Principal Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-retail.com>, ops@acme-retail.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2029 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service handoff: reroute steps and customer verification (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Sarah / Acme ops,

Thanks for validating and switching over — we saw your canary hits come through at 11:02 PDT (trace-id: 7f3b2a0c). That confirms requests are routing to the us-central cluster and error rate dropped from 2.4% -> 0.03% after the change.

Summary and follow-up items: 
- Root cause (preliminary): transient peering flap between a backbone provider and our us-east/eu-west gateways; networking vendor is providing packet-level captures for final RCA.
- Customer impact: partial request loss and increased tail latency for ~95 minutes in affected regions; APAC experienced short-lived increased latency due to global route reconvergence.
- Compensations: we’ve opened temporary-sla-bridge.pdf and noted the incident for billing/credit review.

Planned postmortem and actions (invite attached):
1) Postmortem meeting: Mon, 2029-04-15 09:00 PDT (invite sent).
2) Action items before the meeting:
   - Network vendor to deliver pcap and BGP dump (Markus).
   - Ops to run an expanded canary across 3 additional customers and validate X-Redwood-Trace headers (Marissa).
   - Product to review fallback behavior for long-polling streaming calls (Evelyn / Product).

Sarah — appreciate the fast validation. If you’re available to join the postmortem, we’ll walk through the timeline and planned mitigations. Otherwise, we’ll send notes and the final RCA link to the Drive doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/open?id=postmortem-ACME-20290411

—
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
